commands.name: random_placement
commands.description: Places player starting positions randomly. Mutually exclusive with grouped_by_team and direct_placement.
commands.notes: Sourced from the Definitive RMS Scripting Guide (Zetnus).

commands.name: grouped_by_team
commands.description: Places player starting positions grouped by team.

commands.name: direct_placement
commands.description: Places players directly, in a fixed arrangement rather than randomized.

commands.name: nomad_resources
commands.description: Adds the cost of a town center to every player's starting resources, so a nomad start can build one without gathering wood first. Grants no units and replaces nothing.
commands.notes: guide:379-383. 275 wood and 100 stone on UP/HD; on DE the amount is the player's own civilization's town centre cost, so Incas get 85 extra stone. The previous description ('a nomad-style starting resource/unit set instead of a fixed base') described the nomad GAME MODE rather than this command, and was the only wrong description in this array not already flagged by verified: false.

commands.name: force_nomad_treaty
commands.description: Forces nomad-treaty rules for this map. DE only.

commands.name: behavior_version
commands.description: Selects generation-behavior version for backward compatibility. DE only.

commands.name: override_map_size
commands.description: Overrides the lobby-selected map size with an explicit tile dimension.

arguments.name: size
arguments.description: Values outside this range are clamped.

commands.name: set_gaia_civilization
commands.description: Sets the civilization used for Gaia (neutral) units/buildings on this map. DE only.

commands.name: ai_info_map_type
commands.description: Tells the AI what kind of map this is, affecting its strategy choices.

arguments.name: showType
arguments.description: 0 or 1. UP only - not functional on DE. May be omitted: the engine's arity is three.

commands.notes: Exact behavior differs slightly per game version per the source guide. showType is OMISSIBLE and the engine's arity is THREE - measured 2026-08-11 by RMSTEST_54a/54b. 54a put the three-token form immediately before <LAND_GENERATION>, so an engine expecting a fourth argument would have swallowed the section header and left the map blank; 54b is the same file without the line. Both generated fully snow, so the header survived and nothing was eaten. This reaches the same conclusion as a 2026-08-05 attempt that was reverted the same day, by evidence that attempt could not have had: the flag was marked optional on 52 independent three-argument shipped uses, and reverted because guide:475 lists showType Not functional on DE, so writing it and omitting it are indistinguishable in play and no shipped script could ever have revealed which form is correct. A token-consumption test in game is what settles it, not a headcount. The Hard rules that killed the first attempt stand unchanged.

commands.name: effect_amount
commands.description: Applies a flat-amount gameplay effect (resource/attribute/tech modification) at map start.

arguments.name: amount
arguments.description: DE treats this as a float.

commands.name: effect_percent
commands.description: Same shape as effect_amount, but the value is treated as a percentage (divided by 100).
commands.notes: Made obsolete by Update 141935 (docs/parser-design.md Sec.8). Still parses and still carries its argument shape — the engine accepts it, so this is a note, not an error.

commands.name: guard_state
commands.description: Sets a guard-resource state; only one guard_state is allowed per script.

arguments.name: resourceDelta
arguments.description: DE treats this as a float.

commands.name: terrain_state
commands.description: Sets a UserPatch terrain state. The guide documents it for UP only, so it has no documented effect on DE.
commands.notes: guide:594-612, Game versions: UP only. Arguments and the 0-7 flags range are transcribed from that entry, which is what `verified` records. Whether DE does anything with the command is a SEPARATE and still open question, deliberately kept out of the flag: the guide is silent and nobody has measured it, so the description says only what the guide says. There is no CommandDef field for the guide's per-command `Game versions:` line, which is why this fact has to live in prose.

commands.name: weather_type
commands.description: Sets precipitation and terrain colour tinting on UserPatch. The guide documents it for UP only and points DE authors at color_correction and water_definition instead.
commands.notes: guide:613-637, Game versions: UP only. Precipitation 0 none / 2 rain / 3 thunderstorm / 4 snow, negative reversing the west-to-east direction; liveColor and fogColor are palette indices, 0 meaning no tint. Same split as terrain_state: the argument ranges are verified against the guide, DE behaviour is unmeasured and stays out of the flag.

commands.name: water_definition
commands.description: Selects a named water-type definition (must be #const-defined). DE only.

commands.name: base_terrain
commands.description: Sets the default terrain the whole map starts as, before any lands/terrains are placed.
commands.notes: The same word "base_terrain" is also a valid attribute inside create_elevation/create_terrain blocks — see the attributes[] entry.

commands.name: base_layer
commands.description: Sets a secondary base terrain layer. DE only.

commands.name: enable_waves
commands.description: Toggles shoreline wave visuals. DE only.

commands.name: create_player_lands
commands.description: Creates one land per player, distributing them per the block's attributes. Takes the same attribute set as create_land.

commands.name: create_land
commands.description: Creates one land mass (typically non-player territory — islands, center land, etc). Takes the same attribute set as create_player_lands.

commands.name: create_elevation
commands.description: Raises or lowers terrain elevation in clumps.
commands.notes: maxHeight min corrected 1 -> 0 on 2026-07-31, same cause and same guide phrasing as base_elevation.level: guide:1177 reads "MaxHeight - number (1-16) (default: 0 - not elevated)", so 0 is documented-legal and min 1 contradicted the declared default.

commands.name: cliff_type
commands.description: Sets the visual cliff material for this map. DE only.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: One of CT_GRANITE, CT_DESERT, CT_SNOW, CT_MARBLE, CT_LIMESTONE.

commands.name: min_number_of_cliffs
commands.description: Minimum number of cliff formations to generate.

commands.name: max_number_of_cliffs
commands.description: Maximum number of cliff formations to generate.

commands.name: min_length_of_cliff
commands.description: Minimum length of each cliff formation.
commands.notes: min 3 is DELIBERATE — do not widen it to match corpus usage. guide:1366: "minimum must be at least 3 for cliffs to appear". Six DE-official maps declare 1 or 2 (Fortress.rms:748, Mediterranean.rms:266, Cliffbound.rms:2348, Sandrift.rms:2361, Shrubland.rms:2384, lombardia.rms2:355) and this was briefly read as a false-positive class like circle_radius 0 and base_elevation 0, then reverted 2026-08-05. It is not the same class: those two values are documented as FUNCTIONAL (0 disables circle placement; 0 means not-elevated), so warning on them was wrong. A sub-3 length is documented as NON-functional, so RMS0203 here tells an author their cliff section does nothing — a true positive and one of the more useful warnings we can emit. Corroborating recollection: Fortress declares 5-10 cliffs and is not remembered as having any. Confirm with the three-arm test in preview-design.md Sec.15 item 17b before changing this.

commands.name: max_length_of_cliff
commands.description: Maximum length of each cliff formation.

commands.name: cliff_curliness
commands.description: How often a cliff changes direction along its length — low values for straight cliffs, high for winding ones.
commands.notes: Range/default confirmed; the source guide's fuller description was cut off mid-sentence in the fetch used to populate this file.

commands.name: min_distance_cliffs
commands.description: Minimum distance between separate cliffs, measured in cliff units of 3 tiles. 0 is 0 tiles, 1 is 3 tiles, 2 is 6 tiles.
commands.notes: guide:1388-1393. The cliff-unit scale and the default of 2 were both already hardcoded in src/preview/generator/cliffs.ts (DEFAULT_MIN_DISTANCE_CLIFFS, and the `* 3` at the spacing check) while this entry carried neither, which is the vocabulary-in-code case CLAUDE.md rules out. No `optional` flag: the guide states a default and never states that the command may be omitted from a script that needs it, and a `default:` notation alone does not license omissibility (BUG-003).

commands.name: min_terrain_distance
commands.description: Minimum distance cliffs keep from water, measured in cliff units of 3 tiles. Only water placed in <LAND_GENERATION> counts, since terrain generation runs after cliffs.
commands.notes: guide:1400-1406. The old description said 'certain terrain', which reads as any terrain; the guide says water specifically, and says so twice. The <LAND_GENERATION>-only clause is the guide's own and matters, because a script that paints water in <TERRAIN_GENERATION> gets no cliff avoidance from it at all.

commands.name: color_correction
commands.description: Applies a colour correction preset to the map's lighting. Not visible when the Map Lighting game setting is off, and water is controlled separately by water_definition. DE only.
commands.notes: guide:1424-1436, Game versions: DE only. The argument is a colour correction constant from the guide's Season Types list, with no correction applied when the command is absent.

commands.name: create_terrain

commands.name: create_actor_area
commands.description: Creates an actor area at a fixed map location rather than on an object, with the given identifier and radius, used to constrain later object placement via actor_area_to_place_in/avoid_actor_area.

arguments.name: x
arguments.description: X coordinate in TILES, not a percentage of map width. Must be scaled to map size by hand. May sit outside the map.

arguments.name: y
arguments.description: Y coordinate in TILES, not a percentage of map width. Must be scaled to map size by hand. May sit outside the map.

arguments.name: identifier
arguments.description: Identifier referred to later by actor_area_to_place_in and avoid_actor_area. Multiple actor areas may share one identifier.

commands.notes: Full argument semantics from guide:1982-1996, worked example at guide:1999-2011; supersedes the earlier a/b/c/d stub left unresolved when a source fetch was cut off. Three facts the argument list cannot carry. (1) These fixed-position areas are created BEFORE any create_object command, regardless of where the command sits in the script (guide:1990). That is specific to create_actor_area and does NOT generalise to areas defined by the actor_area ATTRIBUTE on create_object, which come into existence as their objects are placed — guide:2782's rule that several objects sharing one actor_area take the radius of 'the first object successfully created' only means anything if those are built progressively. So avoid_actor_area may reference a create_actor_area identifier declared anywhere in the file, but an attribute-defined one only after that object has been placed. (2) Coordinates are in TILES and must be scaled to map size by hand; off-map coordinates are legal and are the documented way to use a large radius to fence off the map edges (guide:1993). (3) The command CRASHES the game if no lands are generated (guide:1996) — unreachable on a finished map, reachable while editing one.

commands.name: create_object_group

commands.notes: guide:2013-2040, Game versions: DE only. The old description ('places a themed group of objects as a unit') had it backwards in both halves: nothing is placed here, and members are randomised INDIVIDUALLY, so a group must not mix objects with different resource amounts or gameplay effects. Argument retyped objectConstant -> string, matching #const/#define's own name slots: this is a DEFINITION SITE for a name the author invents (the guide calls it text and allows any characters), not a reference to an existing object constant, so RMS0204's 'use a named object constant' and RMS0205's cross-category check were both aimed at the wrong thing. `string` rather than `otherConstant` on purpose - otherConstant is a numeric slot in instantiate.ts, so a group whose name collided with a #const would resolve to a number and silently stop matching the create_object that referenced it.

directives.name: #const
directives.description: Assigns a label to a numeric ID. The value may be a literal number, a math expression, an rnd(), or another constant — everything in the game is a number internally, so constants resolve to their numeric value.
directives.notes: value is typed otherConstant, NOT integer, so that constant-to-constant aliasing (#const PREDATOR_A WOLF) doesn't draw a false RMS0202. Guide L3295 'Everything in the game is represented internally by a numeric identifier' + L3353 'Pre-defined constants will be interpreted as numbers ... where numeric inputs are expected'; L3306 'Items can have multiple constants assigned to them'. otherConstant accepts word OR number (parser-design Sec.6), and expression/rnd handling is ungated by argument type, so #const X (A * B) and #const X rnd(1,5) are unaffected.

directives.name: #undefine
directives.notes: ENGINE-VERIFIED 2026-08-01 by RMSTEST_19_undefine.rms, two runs, both agreeing. (1) #undefine does NOTHING: a flag #define'd then #undefine'd still took its branch (7 of 7 objects placed, against a control of 5 that proved the conditional fires at all). The guide's appendix is right, and validate()'s subsumes() may keep skipping the monotonicity check for negated guards, which is sound only while definitions are irreversible. (2) It does NOT consume the following token: `#undefine base_terrain` followed by `SNOW` produced a 98% SNOW map, so base_terrain survived and ran. The `arguments` array below is therefore NOT a claim about the engine, which reads this as two independent statements. It is kept deliberately, and measured: deleting it makes the operand a separate statement to our parser too, which then reports RMS0200 unknown-command on the flag name of every real #undefine line, including test-maps/sample.rms:16. The array groups the line into the unit the author wrote so RMS0310 can cover all of it at once. `verified` stays false because the arity is a tooling convenience rather than a sourced fact.

directives.name: #include
directives.description: Includes a plain script fragment file.
directives.notes: Confirmed 2026-07-31 against the guide's Non-Functional Syntax appendix, which lists plain #include as an inert engine string; the working directives are #include_drs and #includeXS, documented separately. `verified` stays false for the same reason as #undefine: the appendix sources the name and its inertness, not an argument shape. Note the contrast worth keeping straight — #include_drs really does splice a file in AT THE POINT OF THE DIRECTIVE (the guide's blind-random example puts five of them inside one start_random, which only works in place), so 'include does nothing' is true of this spelling alone.
